sentence: This project builds microfluidic tools to study signaling between human immune cells and fibroblasts and between microbes.
This project uses two real-world groups of patients to study why some people with psoriatic arthritis respond to therapy and others do not.
This project studies which sequence motifs help protein-only biomolecular condensates assemble and how biophysical principles control what they contain.
This project builds immune-based treatments that block HIV infection and help the immune system eliminate HIV-infected cells.
This project develops a 3D-bioprinting technology to build reproducible assembloid structures for studying how interneurons migrate during neurodevelopment.
This project studies how an RNA helicase controls transcription in Ewing sarcoma, a bone cancer.
This project uses deep learning to model retinal vascular topology so that retinopathy of prematurity can be screened more accurately.
This project combines RNA sequencing of lungs from patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and RNA structure probing to find functional RNA structures.
This project creates soft hydrogel microelectrodes that record neural activity from the spinal cord and internal organs while animals move and breathe.
This project tests whether nightshift work impairs whole-body metabolic flexibility and disrupts skeletal muscle clocks, compared with dayshift work.
This project studies how genetic risk scores, biomarkers and neuropathological profiles relate to vulnerability or resistance to Alzheimer's disease.
This project builds a computational framework that automatically checks, documents and updates models of cell signaling using published literature and databases.
This project studies how bioactive molecules from human gut bacteria regulate aging in the host.
This project studies how maternal metabolic status affects early childhood growth and metabolism through placental and breastmilk microRNAs.
This project studies what causes sleep-wake fragmentation in older adults and tests whether afternoon phototherapy reduces its effects on cognition.
This project offers shared services in functional vision assessment, histology and imaging, and bioinformatics to support vision research.
This project studies how chromosomal instability changes gene activity, proteins and immune cells in advanced prostate cancer.
This project studies how herpes simplex virus type 2 changes gene activity in cells of people with HIV and how this helps HIV replicate.
This project develops computational methods that infer population genetics from whole genome data, including spatial population genetics and adaptation.
This project studies how changes in the transcriptome and chromatin states drive lung squamous cell carcinoma and tests a small molecule inhibitor.
